## Summary

I implemented the city title-casing behavior in the owner-creation endpoint (`OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner`).

**Change** — `src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/controller/v1/OwnerRestControllerV1.java`:
- In `addOwner`, after mapping the incoming fields, the city is now resolved via a new `resolveCity(...)` call before duplicate checks and customer-code generation, so the stored and returned `city` reflects the resolved value.
- `resolveCity(String city)`: scans existing owners for one whose city matches the supplied city ignoring case; if found, reuses that owner's exact spelling. Otherwise falls back to a title-cased version. Null-safe.
- `toTitleCase(String value)`: capitalizes the first letter of each whitespace-separated word and lower-cases the rest, preserving original spacing (e.g. `"new york"` / `"NEW YORK"` → `"New York"`).

**Tests** — `OwnerRestControllerV1Tests.java`:
- `createOwnerTitleCasesCity`: a brand-new city (`"west sacramento"`) is returned as `"West Sacramento"`.
- `createOwnerReusesExistingCitySpelling`: with an existing owner in `"OldePortville"`, creating another owner with `"oldeportville"` returns the existing spelling `"OldePortville"`.

V2 has no owner-creation endpoint, so no change was needed there. Existing behavior (duplicate detection, customer code — which already upper-cases the city) is unaffected.
